notes.author: teddy0@snrsiDesktop
notes.content: Maintainer (2026-07-16): this instability alone requires dedicated work — the hybrid smooths the ringing but the solver crashes past t~0.18s (empty-pipe two-phase near-sonic cell over-cools across the (p,h) validity edge). It is the blocker for HybridAllMach being usable; treat as its own future-work item, not a follow-up tweak. HybridAllMach is marked experimental in code until this is resolved.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsiDesktop
notes.content: FIXED 2026-07-16. Root cause: not a physics limit of HEM but a numerical stiffness in the rarefied emptying tail. As the pipe empties past t~0.18s a cell rarefies in a localized runaway (rho 127->23->vacuum over ~350 steps); the conservative-EEqn diagonal rho_cont*V/dt collapses to its 1e-4 floor, the solve becomes ill-conditioned, and one step tips he from 951 kJ/kg to -7.3e6 kJ/kg -> below the 273.15K (p,h) edge -> panic. Both continuity and momentum KNP dissipation independently trigger it, so it is the explicit deferred correction being over-driven in the rarefied tail, not a sign error. Fix: rarefied-tail density taper on the KNP blend beta *= clamp((rho_face-50)/(100-50),0,1), rho_face=min(rho_o,rho_nb). Dissipation zero below 50 kg/m3 (rarefied -> pure PIMPLE, stable), full above 100. Measured min dissipated-face density over the 0-0.15s ringing window is 106.5 kg/m3, so the taper is inert there. Results: full 600ms HybridAllMach completes (no panic/NaN, void in [0,1]), plateau 387.7 psia, GS-1 RMSE 30.6 psia, no cold tail; 0-0.15s ringing -55.5% and plateau retained bit-identically; default Pimple bit-identical (920 lib tests pass). See collaboration/edwards_tampines_regen/hybrid_stability_debug_log.md + figures_hybrid_stable/. Not committed (maintainer commits).

title: Hybrid all-Mach: harden full-600ms Edwards run past t~0.18s (empty-pipe two-phase near-sonic over-cool)

description: Port REAL cyclic-patch support into outram-foam-basic-lib. Investigation (2026-08-04): PatchKind::Cyclic is DECLARED (mesh/fv_mesh.rs:79 'Periodic / matching pair') and round-trips through polyMesh I/O (io/poly_mesh.rs:406/419 parse+write 'cyclic'), but is NOT wired into the FV operators or matrix assembly — grep finds Cyclic only in the enum decl, a doc comment, and the I/O string map; nothing in fvm::div / fvm::laplacian pairs cyclic faces or adds the across-boundary neighbour coupling. This is why the moltres MSR port (op-6w0.3) could not use it and fell back to a ring-of-internal-faces workaround. Deliverable: implement cyclic face-pairing (owner<->neighbour across the matching patch pair) in the FV discretisation so periodic domains work natively — required for a real 2-D/3-D MSR core coupled to a 1-D external loop. Scope: face-pair topology on Cyclic patch pairs, operator contributions (div/laplacian/interpolate) across the pair, matrix off-diagonal coupling, and a V&V case (e.g. 1-D advection/diffusion on a periodic ring matching the analytic periodic solution).

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: Implemented cyclic (periodic) patch support (2026-08-04). Representation: cyclic pairing stored as BoundaryPatch::cyclic_partner (partner patch index, half0/half1 same-local-index correspondence) + FvMesh::cyclic_couplings (Vec<CyclicCoupling> of owner<->neighbour cell couplings), derived at build time; FvMesh::periodic_1d builds a 1-D periodic ring programmatically. Coupling assembled by APPENDING one LDU face per seam pair after the internal faces (FvMatrix/FvVectorMatrix::new pre-allocate the slots so all matrices on a mesh share structure and +/- line up); laplacian(_vec)/div(_vec) fill them with the internal-face formula (coeff=Gamma*|Sf|/d_seam, d_seam=|Cf_A-C_ownerA|+|Cf_B-C_ownerB|; upwind on seam flux). fvc interpolate/sn_grad use the paired cell across the seam. Non-cyclic behaviour byte-identical. V&V (verification, untrusted AI draft pending human review): cyclic diffusion == all-internal regular-n-gon ring mesh (operators identical A.x to <1e-12; solved fields agree <1e-9); periodic advection conserves (A.ones=0) and == ring; interpolate/sn_grad/vector-Laplacian seam checks. Both gates green: --lib 284 passed, --doc 25 passed (release). Honest scope: polyMesh parser does NOT yet read cyclic neighbourPatch ordering (must wire programmatically); DIC-PCG/GAMG not tuned for the appended seam faces (use Gauss-Seidel for cyclic, which is order-independent); first-pass orthogonal seam only.

title: outram-foam-basic-lib: implement cyclic (periodic) patch support in the FV operators + matrix assembly

acceptance_criteria: CLAUDE.md states the Termux hard rule (done); every non-GUI lib crate builds under a native Termux cargo build.
description: Elevated Android portability to a hard rule in root CLAUDE.md (## Android / Termux portability): every crate's non-GUI library code MUST compile on a native, on-device Termux build (target_os="android", aarch64-linux-android, no NDK cross-toolchain, no system BLAS/LAPACK, no C/Fortran toolchain). Android-hostile deps/tests/examples must be held off behind Android feature gates + cfg(target_os="android") in the SAME change that introduces them. Acceptance bar = a build run inside Termux succeeds for every non-GUI library. GUI (egui/eframe/windowing) stays out of unconditional library builds. This bead tracks the rule itself (codified); per-crate verification is op-zfr.2 and the native-Termux sweep below.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: Hard rule hardened in root CLAUDE.md (commit c4b3949) with two lessons from the on-device godiva failure: (1) the portability check MUST be --all-targets (or a native Termux build), never --lib-only, because --lib silently skips examples/tests/benches; (2) examples/bins need an Android stub main under cfg(target_os="android") + per-item gating of desktop items, whereas tests/benches can blank the whole file with #![cfg(not(target_os="android"))]. Precedents cited in the rule: njoy gpu_wmp_bench, outram-mc godiva_gpu_benchmark, outram-foam-basic-lib tests/matrix_bench.

title: HARD RULE: non-GUI library code must compile natively on Termux (android feature gates)
